name: wizwick
description: Study packs from your own notes in any subject, with short lessons, practice cards, a quiz and a study plan, plus hands-on activities right in the chat.

interface.longDescription:
wizWick turns what you're studying into a study pack. Attach your notes, a study guide, a manual, slides, worksheets or photos of them, in any subject: biology, history, a new language, flight school, an IT certification. Then ask for a study pack.

Your pack has a few short sessions, each with a short lesson and practice cards, then a practice quiz and a study plan. For some subjects a session opens with a hands-on activity, like solving equations on wizWick's Algebra balance or building lines on a graph. Anything your materials don't make clear is listed for you to ask your teacher or instructor about.

Tap Open in wizWick to study the pack on wizwick.com, on a phone or a computer, and add it to your library to keep it. Stuck on a card? Come back to the chat, say which session and card, and work it through step by step.

Learn by doing, right in the chat. Type an equation, like 3x + 7 = 22, and solve it on wizWick's Algebra balance. Or ask for a hands-on activity: the Atom Builder and Gold Foil for chemistry; Line Lab, Algebra Tiles, the Number Line, the Function Machine, Parabola Lab, Exponent Lab and Growth Lab for math; and the Growing Map of the United States for history. Each one comes with a short set of challenges that check your work.

wizWick doesn't keep your files. A pack is only saved when you add it to your wizWick account.
defaultPrompt: Make me a study pack from my notes
Open the Atom Builder so I can practice isotopes

positive.description: Make a study pack from pasted biology notes
positive.prompt: Make me a study pack from these notes: Cell structure. All living things are made of cells. Prokaryotic cells, like bacteria, have no nucleus; eukaryotic cells (plants, animals, fungi) do. The nucleus holds the cell's DNA. Mitochondria release energy from glucose in cellular respiration. Ribosomes make proteins. The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves. Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts for photosynthesis and a large central vacuole. Test on Friday.
positive.expected_behavior: A study pack card appears with 2 to 4 sessions, practice cards, a practice quiz and an Open in wizWick button. Open in wizWick opens the pack on wizwick.com without signing in.

positive.description: Make a study pack for a subject outside school
positive.prompt: Turn these ground school notes into a study pack: Airspace classes. Class A starts at 18,000 feet MSL and needs an IFR clearance. Class B surrounds the busiest airports, and you need a clearance to enter it. Class C needs two-way radio contact with ATC before you enter. Class D usually surrounds an airport with a tower, up to about 2,500 feet above it, and needs two-way radio contact. Class E is controlled airspace that isn't A, B, C or D. Class G is uncontrolled.
positive.expected_behavior: A study pack card appears for the airspace classes, built from the notes, with an Open in wizWick button.
wizWick's Algebra opens in the chat with 3x + 7 = 22 on a balance. Dragging the 7 and then the 3 across solves it step by step, and the balance shows x = 5.

positive.description: Open a hands-on chemistry activity with a chosen set of challenges
positive.prompt: Open the Atom Builder so I can practice isotopes.
positive.expected_behavior: The Atom Builder opens in the chat with its isotopes and mass number challenges. Tapping C in the periodic table builds carbon-12 and passes the first challenge.
The wizWick welcome card appears: how to make a study pack from your own materials, and the hands-on activities like wizWick's Algebra, the Atom Builder, Line Lab and the Growing Map.

publication.release_notes: First public release: study packs from your own materials in any subject, opened on wizwick.com; wizWick's Algebra balance for linear equations; ten hands-on activities in the chat, like the Atom Builder, Line Lab and the Growing Map, each with challenges; a welcome card.
